summary.headline: CERA Q2 FY27 revenue rose 27.4% YoY to INR 603 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 12.2% from 14.2% a year ago.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 27.4% YoY to INR 603 crore, driven mainly by volume (about 16.6 percentage points of the growth), with price contributing about 9.1 points. EBITDA excluding other income rose to INR 73 crore, but the margin of 12.2% was below last year's 14.2% and above Q1 FY27's 10.1%. Brass cost was up 58% YoY and gas cost up about 40%, and PAT was flat at INR 56 crore. Management reiterated a FY27 EBITDA margin of 13-14% and said revenue growth should exceed the 18-20% target, with H2 margin recovery depending on price realisation and discount reversal.

segments.name: Sanitaryware
segments.commentary: 45% of Q2 revenue, grew 24% YoY (volume 14.3%, price 6.7%, mix 2.7% per management's bridge; sanitaryware revenue growth stated as 23.7%). Plant utilisation about 82%.

segments.name: Faucetware
segments.commentary: 43% of Q2 revenue, grew 38% YoY (volume about 24%, price 10.3%, mix 1.9%). Monthly capacity raised from 4 lakh to 5 lakh units from September 2026 via added equipment in the same facility.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth now expected to surpass the earlier 18-20% target, per management.
FY27 EBITDA margin outlook of 13-14% maintained; CFO said the guidance was marginally revised downward on the call, per an analyst's remark.
Management expects margin to improve progressively in H2 FY27, from pricing actions, cost efficiency and volume growth.

Bridge: Q1 margin 10.1% plus one-time reversal ~3.8pp and price ~1pp plus operating leverage 1.9pp implied 16.8%; negative items of -4.6pp (brass -2.1, publicity -0.5, procurement -0.3, discounts -1.7) brought it to 12.2%.
Project-to-retail mix expected to stabilise around 40:60; Q2 was 39:61 versus 43:57 in Q1.
Capex: INR 27 crore spent in H1 FY27 against a full-year plan of about INR 43 crore.
No FY28 revenue guidance; management will give it after FY27 closes.
No further price increases planned for Q3 FY27 per management; faucetware price hike of about 8% from 1 September 2026 expected to flow through from late Q3.
capex_capacity: Faucetware capacity raised from 4 lakh to 5 lakh pieces per month from September 2026 by adding balancing equipment; can go to 6-7 lakh in phases if demand supports, to be reviewed in Q4 FY27.
Sanitaryware utilisation about 82% in Q2; a greenfield sanitaryware project is pending, land already procured, with a decision expected by end of Q4 FY27.
H1 FY27 capex INR 27 crore against full-year plan of about INR 43 crore.
Sourcing mix: sanitaryware 41% in-house and 59% outsourced; faucetware 55% in-house and 45% outsourced. Management plans to shift more sanitaryware volume in-house.
demand_pricing: Volume-led growth: management said pre-buying from two price hikes was not the main driver; the company believes it gained market share over the last three to four quarters.

Price: sanitaryware took about 12% in May 2026; faucetware took 16% in May plus about 8% in September 2026 (total 24%). Outsourced procurement costs rose about 12% (9% in April/May and 3% in September).
Retail rose to 61% of revenue; projects 39%. Growth was consistent across July, August and September.
Brass averaged INR 932/kg in Q2 (up 58% YoY, 11% QoQ); gas averaged INR 47.29/cubic metre (up from INR 33.79). Management said freight is 11-12% of sanitaryware revenue and 8-9% for the company.
Management said it is not seeing price cuts even if inputs fall; higher discounts would be the pass-through route in a weak-demand scenario.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of growth into volume, price and mix, and drivers of volume (market share, pre-buying?).
qa_highlights.answer: Company growth was 16.6% volume, 9.1% price and 1.7% mix. Management attributed volume to genuine demand and distribution efforts, not just pre-buying, and said share gains are likely but hard to measure given unlisted peers.

qa_highlights.question: Will the project share fall to 40% immediately, and are old low-margin orders still running?
qa_highlights.answer: Project share was already 39% in Q2 versus 43% in Q1, which was an aberration from accelerated deliveries. Some old-price orders continue into Q3, with mostly new-priced projects from late Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Can H2 margin of about 14.5% be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management walked through a bridge from 10.1% in Q1 to 12.2% in Q2 and said the -1.7pp discount drag and the faucetware price hike should reverse in Q3-Q4, so 13-14% full-year margin should be achievable.

qa_highlights.question: Geopolitics: is there a shift from unorganised to organised players?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the situation is double-edged: gas prices are higher but available, Morbi players are partly impacted, and some consumers are moving toward branded products; gains are mainly attributed to company initiatives.

qa_highlights.question: Brand mix and CERA brand share of revenue.
qa_highlights.answer: Premium/mid/entry split (43/37/rest) is not by brand. CERA brand is about 98-99% of revenue; Senator and POLIPLUZ together are about INR 70 crore for the year. FY27 revenue expectation cited as about INR 2,450 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Will prices be rolled back if input costs fall, and any further price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect price rollbacks; any relief would show up as higher discounts or project pricing. No further price increase is planned for Q3 FY27.

risks_watch: Brass (INR 932/kg in Q2, about 60-65% of faucetware COGS) and gas costs remain elevated; a gas cost doubling hits outsourcing partners, who supply about 55% of sanitaryware volume.
Discount drag of 1.7pp in Q2 from fixed-price legacy projects and retail schemes; reversal timing depends on scheme roll-off.
Dependence on outsourcing (about 50% of volume per management) limits capacity to meet demand; Morbi supplier stress.
FY28 revenue guidance deferred; management cited external uncertainty and the geopolitical situation.
Q3 FY27 margin: whether the faucetware price hike and discount reversal lift margin to the implied H2 level.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume momentum and on reaching the 13-14% full-year margin, but cautious on the input cost outlook and deferred FY28 guidance. Management explained the Q2 margin shortfall in detail with a quantified bridge, and was less specific on the sanitaryware pricing and cost recovery timeline.
key_quotes: We are now confident of surpassing the revenue growth target, along with the full year's EBITDA margin outlook of 13%-14%.
So, we expect that the negative discount factor of -1.7% will disappear and also improved pricing will further come into play.
Even then, we do not anticipate a kind of a rollback in prices, because even now, you find there is a lot of impact on the profitability.

Greenfield sanitaryware project (land procured, decision by end Q4 FY27; not yet approved)

growth.why: Management says FY27 revenue growth will surpass the 18-20% target, backed by volume-led demand, two price hikes and a faucetware capacity increase to 5 lakh/month from September 2026, though sanitaryware utilisation is 82% and the greenfield plant is only at the decision stage; EBITDA margin guide of 13-14% was held but the CFO reportedly revised it marginally down.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin was 12.2% vs 10.1% in Q1, and management expects H2 recovery to the 13-14% FY27 range from discount reversal (-1.7pp drag) and the 8% faucetware price hike from 1 Sept 2026, though brass (INR 932/kg, up 58% YoY) and gas costs remain elevated.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2 FY27 live; Q4 FY27 review for more
rows.why: Faucetware capacity already raised from 4 to 5 lakh pieces/month from Sept 2026 (+25%), with 6-7 lakh possible in phases, to be reviewed in Q4 FY27; sanitaryware utilisation at 82% with greenfield project pending a decision by end Q4 FY27 (not yet approved).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 volume contributed 16.6pp of the 27.4% revenue growth, faucetware volume up about 24%, and management expects FY27 revenue growth to surpass the 18-20% target.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Sanitaryware utilisation at 82% with a greenfield project on land already procured and a decision expected by end Q4 FY27; H1 capex INR 27 crore vs full-year plan of about INR 43 crore.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management says FY27 revenue growth will surpass the 18-20% target, but EBITDA margin guidance of 13-14% was only held (and CFO reportedly revised it marginally down), so a margin upgrade is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Brass up 58% YoY and gas up about 40%, outsourced costs up about 12%, and Q2 margin at 12.2% sits below the 13-14% FY27 range; H2 must average about 14.5% to hit the range, and FY28 guidance is deferred.

rows.label: Faucetware price hike of about 8% from 1 Sept 2026 flows through late Q3
rows.why: Faucetware had 16% in May plus about 8% in September (24% total), and the September hike is expected to lift margin from late Q3; no further price increase is planned for Q3 FY27.

rows.label: Net working capital days down to 58 from 77
rows.why: Inventory fell to 69 days from 83 and receivables to 28 days from 33, with cash at INR 897 crore at 30 Sep 2026.

rows.label: Shift sanitaryware volume in-house from 41%
rows.why: Sanitaryware is 41% in-house and 59% outsourced, and outsourced partners are exposed to gas and brass cost spikes; management plans to shift more volume in-house.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume momentum and the 13-14% full-year margin, and gave a detailed Q1-to-Q2 margin bridge, but was cautious on input costs and deferred FY28 guidance. Analysts probed the H2 margin path, the project-to-retail mix, and whether the CFO had trimmed the margin guide.
